newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares notch small gains in six-day rally.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares notch small gains in six-day rally.

text.p: ** Indian stocks close with small gains as
profit-taking caps a sharp mid-session rally --traders
** Bombay stocks index up 12.43 points, or 0.32 pct at
3,873.85, off 3,901.45 --intra-day high
** Market focus on buying by foreign funds in select stocks
** Diversified firm, Raymonds drops 10 percent to 54.75
rupees after company posts plunge in 1996/97 net profit
** Term-lender IDBI announces slightly higher 1996/97 net
profit, stock ends little changed
** Delhi index down 1.99 pts at 809.48, Madras up 12.14 pts
at 3,685.83 and Calcutta crawls 0.01 pts up at 109.43
Indian stocks ended with marginal higher on Thursday after a round of profit-taking capped a mid-session rally, traders said.
"There has been select enquiries by foreign funds," said Kirti Doshi, dealer at Bombay's Biyani Securities. "Multinational, banking and petroleum stocks were in market fancy."
A sharp afternoon rally which helped Bombay's benchmark 30-share index gain nearly one percent attracted a bout of profit-taking, participants said.
Bombay shares have added nearly 184 points, or nearly five percent, in six straight sessions on the back of renewed buying by foreign funds.
"The market still looks healthy. Shares have seen a steady rise in this rally," said Neeraj Roy, head of institutional sales at Prime Broking.
Foreign funds were buyers in refinery stocks -- HPCL, BPCL, GAIL and ONGC, multinationals -- Hindustan Lever, Colgate, Nestle and Glaxo, traders said.
Among company results, term-lender Industrial Development Bank of India posted a slighty higher 1996/97 net profit.

IDBI announced a net profit of 11.44 billion rupees in the year ending March 31, 1997 against 10.07 billion in the year-ago period. The firm raised its dividend to 3.5 rupees a share from three rupees last year. Shares of IDBI ended 0.50 rupees down at 91.75 on volumes of 72,800 shares at the Bombay exchange.
Analysts on Thursday said India's economy, hamstrung by lacklustre industrial growth and sluggish exports, is expected to stage a recovery but not before late 1997.
The Commerce Ministry on Wednesday reported that exports -- critical to India's growth -- plunged 10.1 percent in April to $2.52 billion from $2.81 billion in the same month last year.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
